items.title: A Hiker Fell off a Cliff in Big Bend National Park. Then Rescuers Had to Leave Him There Overnight.
items.summary:
A 19-year-old hiker is safe after falling off a cliff and staying the night on a narrow ledge in Big Bend National Park , one of the most remote national parks in the Lower 48.

According to a news release, on November 13, the man, whose name authorities have not released, fell ten feet when his gear gave way out in an area inaccessible to ground-based search and rescue responders. Rescuers reached the area just after 9 P.M. and called the Georgia Army National Guard medical evacuation crew assigned to the Joint Task Force-Southern Border. The organization works with U.S. Customs and Border Protection to monitor the shared border between Texas and Mexico, an area central to a heated national debate over the Trump Administration’s border wall construction .

The helicopter crew had taken off, but with limited lighting and winds approaching 35 miles per hour, and a string of storms moving into the area, the Black Hawk medevac crew made the difficult decision to scrub the mission.

“The crew agreed it was not safe and we had to make the unfortunate decision to go back and try again in the daylight,” Chief Warrant Officer 2 Gregory Hiett, the aircraft commander, said in a statement . “It was an extremely difficult thing to do, knowing the patient was going to be stuck out there for the rest of the night.”

Throughout the night, park responders remained on-scene and on the ground.

Just after 9 A.M. on November 14, a second helicopter mission launched with a hoist rescue team. Flight medic and technician Holly Johnson descended 150 feet on a cable, determined the hiker was…
items.t: A Hiker Fell off a Cliff in Big Bend National Park. Then Rescuers Had to Leave Him There Overnight.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 Is Here. Goodbye, Winter Training Plan.
items.summary:
On my run this morning, the streets of New York seemed a little emptier. You may have noticed the same thing in your part of the world. It is not the Rapture. It’s Grand Theft Auto .

Across the country, a lot of people have come down with a sudden and very specific illness. Even the man who profits from it saw this coming. Back in April, Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick said, “I think a lot of people will be calling in sick on November 19.” One economist puts the cost in lost productivity at around $1 billion. To be fair, it’s been a long wait. GTA V came out 13 years ago. My daughter was in daycare then. (That was the only time I could sneak in some game time.) She is now a freshman in high school.

Here’s the thing, though: for a game about crime, a surprising amount of it is about nature. I mean, there’s a National Park you can explore. It’s been less than 24 hours, and my Instagram feed has already served up players feeding NPCs (the game’s random bystanders) to alligators and a Bigfoot lurking near a swamp called Cottonmouth Lake. The Bigfoot is the Skunk Ape of actual Florida folklore. It knocks you out with noxious fumes, and the last thing you see is a pair of giant hairy feet coming toward you. In its demented way, it’s a Florida nature documentary. Which is to say: you are about to lose a lot of people to the swamp.

Then there’s the time commitment. Rockstar Games says one of its studio heads needed about 80 hours to get through the story, side quests included. That’s a 16-week marathon build at five hours a week. For those of us with a training plan to execute, a…
items.t: Grand Theft Auto 6 Is Here. Goodbye, Winter Training Plan.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 Has an Entire National Park. I Spent the Night Exploring It.
items.summary:
Many gamers have waited 13 years for a new Grand Theft Auto (GTA)  game so they can steal cars, rob banks, and wreak havoc in a fictional American city. I had a slightly different mission. I wanted to go hiking.

GTA VI , the long-awaited installment in Rockstar Games’ blockbuster franchise, arrived November 19 with an enormous open world set in Leonida, a fictional state modeled after Florida. Beyond the game’s cities and beaches are mangrove swamps, forested mountains, and a surprising number of opportunities for outdoor recreation.

Among them is an entire national park that some fans believe was inspired by Georgia’s Providence Canyon State Park . Naturally, as a journalist who covers the outdoors, I decided to investigate.

Getting there was its own expedition. I spent several hundred dollars on a PlayStation 5 specifically for this assignment, endured a download that initially threatened to take 14 hours, and worked through introductory missions involving a robbery and a dubious boating operation before I could drive north to the game’s national park—Mount Kalaga.

Welcome to Mount Kalaga National Park 
 Grand Theft Auto VI features more than 170 animal species across its fictional state of Leonida. (Photo: Courtesy of Rockstar Games) 
 Located near Leonida’s northern border, Mount Kalaga is one of six major regions players can explore, with a vast stretch of mountainous backcountry offering hunting, fishing, and off-road trails, according to Rockstar’s official description . It took me about 20 minutes of real-life driving to get there from the game’s starting…

items.title: A Teen Hiker Needed Rescue on a Popular Tahoe Peak. An Expert Explains Why Snow Makes It Dangerous.
items.summary:
Search and rescue volunteers saved a 17-year-old hiker missing on California’s Mount Tallac on November 16 after following bootprints through the snow for hours.

The teenager, whose name authorities have not released, showed early signs of hypothermia when responders found him in rugged terrain away from the established hiking trail, the El Dorado County Sheriff’s Office wrote in a statement .

“The Sheriff’s Office is grateful that this search and rescue effort had a positive outcome,” the agency wrote. “However, situations like this can quickly turn tragic, particularly in challenging winter conditions.”

Located near South Lake Tahoe, Mount Tallac reaches an elevation of 9,739 feet. And in November, high-elevation conditions can deteriorate rapidly.

“In inclement weather, especially later in the day when it starts getting dark, it’s tough to find your way if you don’t already know the terrain,” Jared Manninen, a local outdoor writer and founder of the website Tahoe T rail Gu ide , told Outside. 

Mount Tallac is one of the most popular summit hikes in Lake Tahoe’s Desolation Wilderness , a nearly 64,000-acre expanse of federally protected backcountry in the Sierra Nevada, but it also draws search-and-rescue calls year after year. The ten-mile trail climbs roughly 3,500 feet through steep, rocky terrain that becomes especially difficult to navigate once snow covers the route.

Even on a well-traveled route like the Mount Tallac Trail, a few inches of snow can make the trail much harder to find, especially on the descent.

items.title: Supermoon Season Is Coming. Here’s Where to Watch in Every Single State.
items.summary:
Thanksgiving week will bring the first supermoon since January 2026. It kicks off a series of not one but four oversized full moons in a row, including the closest supermoon of the decade thus far in December. While you can admire the bright sphere throughout the night, a few specific tips and tricks will dramatically improve your view—including strategizing when and where to watch.

I’ve chased at least a dozen supermoons as an astrophotographer and night-sky tourist , from the badlands of South Dakota to Serengeti National Park in Tanzania. In this guide, I’m sharing everything you need to know as we enter supermoon season, including timing logistics and guidance on where to watch the luminous sphere in every state.

Sunset is one of the best times to see an epic supermoon (Photo: Stephanie Vermillion) 
 How to See the Next Supermoon 
 The Thanksgiving-week supermoon will hit on Tuesday, November 24 It reaches full illumination that morning, but there’s an even better time to view it: sunset.

The round orb looks especially large and bright as it rises and sets due to an effect known as the moon illusion. A supermoon can appear up to 30 percent brighter and 14 percent bigger than the smallest full moon. Near the horizon, it looks even more gargantuan. If you’re hoping to snag supermoon photos, moonrise and moonset are the times to do it.

The full moon rises in the east to northeast as the sun sets in the west, and sinks in the west as the morning sun appears out east. The golden hour hues only add to the drama, turning the globe a tangerine tinge.

items.t: Supermoon Season Is Coming. Here’s Where to Watch in Every Single State.

items.title: New Research Shows Why Running Takes More Energy as We Get Older
items.summary:
Running can get harder as you age . Normal wear and tear takes a toll, and your body needs more energy to cover the same distance.

A new study, published in the Journal of Experimental Biology in November 2026, found that some muscles in older runners were weaker than those in younger runners. Other muscles overcompensated for those weaknesses.

“The aging process leads to decreased strength and volume of muscles, including the calf muscles involved in plantarflexion,” Changal T. Nguyen, MD , a sports medicine physiatrist, told Outside .

Dr. Nguyen is also a clinical assistant professor of orthopedic surgery at Stanford and was not involved in the study. “The calf muscles and Achilles tendon also become less stiff with age, so they work less effectively as a spring, she said.

The good news, Dr. Nguyen said, is that adding a few simple exercises to your routine can help keep your calves strong and your Achilles tendon functioning well as you age.

How the Muscles in Your Feet and Legs Start to Work Differently as You Age 
 The authors of the new study recruited 18 runners with an average age of 26.1 years and 18 runners with an average age of 63.4 years. The study referred to each group as “young athletes” and “master athletes,” respectively.

The researchers measured the athletes’ Achilles tendon stiffness and plantar flexor movements. (The plantar flexor muscles—located in the feet, ankles , and calves— propel you forward and upward as you run .) Then, both groups completed two six-minute treadmill sessions at two different speeds—roughly 5.6 miles per hour (mph) and…
items.t: New Research Shows Why Running Takes More Energy as We Get Older

items.title: Hannah Otto Broke Her Leg Descending Kilimanjaro—and Kept Riding
items.summary:
By the time professional mountain biker Hannah Otto, 30, reached the final miles of her descent from Mount Kilimanjaro, 19,341 feet, she had already navigated the mountain’s most punishing terrain. She’d hauled her bike up snowy slopes, scrambled over boulders at 18,000 feet, and ridden steep, rocky trails where softball-sized stones shifted beneath her tires. Now she was on a rainforest dirt road easy enough to ride on a gravel bike.

On November 3, Otto became the first known woman to ascend and descend Africa’s tallest mountain with a bicycle in a single day. She completed the effort in 10 hours, 18 minutes, and 51 seconds, despite breaking her leg just two miles from the finish.

“I came around a gentle bend in the trail, and the trail went from dry dirt to mud, and it was like I hit ice,” Otto told Outside. “The bike just came out from underneath me, and I was on the ground in a second.”

The fall had broken her leg. But two miles from the finish, she got back on her bike and rode out.

The attempt was also part of a fundraising campaign for World Bicycle Relief , a nonprofit that provides bicycles to improve access to education, healthcare, and employment. Otto hopes to raise $165,000 to provide 1,000 bicycles to rural African communities.

Otto carries her mountain bike across a snow-covered section of Kilimanjaro. The upper slopes were too steep to ride, forcing her to carry the bike for roughly three miles.
